_doc: Lessons are one event, not a wait (Week autoload): when a class block starts and you're in the school, pick how you spend it and the clock jumps to the end of the block (morning: homeroom -> 12:30 lunch, afternoon: 13:20 -> 15:20). Late = arrived after 8:30. Truancy = in town 15+ minutes into a block. subjects.<weekday> = [morning, afternoon]. results.<choice> = lines ({subject}).
open: {block}: {subject}. The windows are fogged with rain. Hayate is already drawing a dog in the margin.
{block}: {subject}. The class rep, Sato Yui, hands out worksheets with a perfect smile.
{block}: {subject}. Chalk dust drifts in a stripe of thin sunlight. Somewhere below, a bell rings by itself.
{block}: {subject}. Through the door's little window, a black hood passes. Then passes again.
late: You slide the door open {late} minutes late. Makabe-sensei looks at the clock, then at you, then writes something down. "Sit, Asagiri."
Late. Thirty heads turn. Hayate gives you a thumbs-up. Makabe-sensei gives you a long sigh and a tick in his book.
You creep in {late} minutes late. Nobody says anything. The silence says it for them.

attend: You actually follow {subject} for once. Your notes are almost readable.
Makabe-sensei reads a love letter from the Heian period aloud and his voice cracks on the last line. Nobody laughs.
You answer a question correctly. Hayate looks at you as if you'd betrayed him.
You learn something. You forget it by lunch. It still counts.
The lesson is slow, but for a while the rain is only rain.
doze: You dream of a summer you don't remember: sunflowers, a girl with a camera, a bell. You wake up with ink on your cheek.
You sleep through {subject}. A piece of chalk bounces off your head. Makabe-sensei has excellent aim.
You doze off and dream you are much smaller, waiting on a very long staircase. Someone shakes you awake. It's the bell.
Hayate covers for you by asking a very long question about nothing. Good friend.
window: Down in the courtyard, 1-A has PE. One small figure in a black hood is not running. He is looking up at your window.
A black cat sits on the wall by the gate for the whole lesson, staring at the school. It doesn't blink once.
The shrine on the hill is lost in cloud. For a second you think you hear its bell, all the way down here.
Rain runs down the glass in lines. One of them, for a moment, looks like a cat's paw print.
A white heron lands on the school fence, looks at you, and leaves. You don't know why that feels like a warning.
note: You pass Hayate a note. He writes back: "MELON BREAD AFTER?" with a drawing of a dog eating a melon bread.
Hayate's reply comes back folded into a tiny dog. It just says "you ok?". You didn't know you looked otherwise.
The note gets caught. Makabe-sensei reads it aloud: "is the hood kid outside again". He folds it neatly and keeps it. He keeps everything.

truant: {block} started without you. Somewhere, Makabe-sensei writes 'absent' in very small, very sad handwriting.
You're not in class. Your phone buzzes: Hayate - "bro where are you". Then Amane - "Senpai isn't in his seat."
The school bell rings across the river. You're on the wrong side of it.

consequence.late_3: Aunt Haruka is waiting at the counter with a letter from the school. "Three times late in one week, Toru." She doesn't shout. She just gives you a mochi with no filling, which is worse.
consequence.truant_2: Makabe-sensei phoned the shop. Aunt Haruka says nothing at dinner, which she has never done before. Later, through the wall, you hear her on the phone to Tokyo.

open: EXAM: {subject}. Makabe-sensei hands out the papers face down. "Begin." Thirty pencils scratch at once. The rain taps the window like someone counting.
EXAM: {subject}. The clock above the blackboard is loud enough to hear. Hayate is already sweating. Sato Yui has already finished the first page.
EXAM: {subject}. A black hood passes the door's little window twice. Makabe-sensei draws the blind without looking up.

choices.t: Guess the ones you don't know and move on.
Slide your answers where Hayate can see them.
Watch the clock and pace yourself.
Copy from Sato Yui's paper. She always finishes first.

results.careful: You work through it line by line. Some of it you actually know.
results.guess: You circle answers by feel. Your feel is not very well educated.
results.help: Hayate sees. Hayate copies. Hayate copies your name too, then frantically rubs it out. Makabe-sensei sighs at the ceiling and says nothing.
results.clock: You split the time evenly and finish with two minutes spare. You use them to look out of the window.
results.copy_ok: Sato Yui's paper is tilted toward you like an invitation. You copy six answers, then nine. Nobody looks up. On your left shoulder, something very small giggles.
results.copy_caught: Makabe-sensei's hand lands on your paper. He doesn't shout. He just writes a zero at the top, very neatly, and says "See me after school, Asagiri." Thirty pencils stop at once.

grades.A: The paper comes back with a red circle and a tiny drawn cat. Aunt Haruka pins it to the shop wall.
grades.B: Respectable. Makabe-sensei writes "Good. Sleep more." in the margin.
grades.C: Passable. Aunt Haruka says "Your father got Cs too," and then looks like she wishes she hadn't.
grades.D: Red ink everywhere. Hayate got the same mark and wants to high-five about it.
grades.F: Zero. Makabe-sensei keeps you after class and talks for an hour about trust, in a quiet voice that is much worse than shouting. Aunt Haruka gets a phone call.

_doc_exams: Exam prep (Week): `exam_hint` = objective line when exams are 1-4 days away. cram.<library|home> = studying at the school library (2F) or your desk at home (1 h, Study +3; tired = +1 in 90 min; 3 a day). tutor.<id> = a friend tutors you (People menu, 90 min) or you drill Hayate. Exam choice `copy`: caught by chance (agility, courage, see-through), grade F. ranking.* = the board after the last exam day ({rank}).
exam_hint: Exams in {n} day(s): cram at the library (2F) or your desk at home, or ask a friend to tutor you.
exam_hint_today: Exams today: what you studied counts.

library: The library smells of dust and radiator heat. Three third-years asleep on their textbooks. You open yours.
The librarian stamps your card without looking up. 'Exam season,' she says, as if it's weather.
A whole table to yourself, by the window. Rain on the glass. The perfect place to study, or to stare.
home: Your desk at home: a lamp, a cold cup of tea, Grandpa's old pencil case. Downstairs, Aunt Haruka is watching a quiz show and shouting the answers.
Your room smells of tatami and eraser shavings. A cat sits on the windowsill outside, watching you study like a supervisor.
cram.amane: Let Amane quiz you. (He's been waiting by the door.)
cram.done: Your eyes won't focus any more. You've done all you can today.
result: You read the same page three times and the third time it stays.
Formulas, dates, kanji. Some of it sticks. You can feel it sticking.
An hour of work. Your hand is grey with pencil.
cram.tired: You wake up with your cheek on the textbook and a page printed backwards on your face. Ninety minutes gone, a little learned.
amane_result: Amane quizzes you from the flashcards he made. He made a hundred and twelve. Each one has a tiny cat drawn in the corner. He blushes every time you get one right.
"Senpai, the Meiji Restoration was 1868. ...I know because I was there. A-a joke! It was a joke." You remember the date forever after that.

reiji.ask: "Could you help me study for the exams?"
reiji.yes: Reiji takes you to the council room and teaches like he runs the council: no wasted words, a timetable, a red pen. "Again," he says, eleven times. You learn more in ninety minutes than in a month.
reiji.no: "I don't tutor people I don't know." (Get closer to Reiji first.)

hina.yes: Hina turns the syllabus into a newspaper: headlines for every chapter, 'SHOCKING: MITOCHONDRIA IS THE POWERHOUSE'. It works. You can't forget a headline.
hina.no: "Ehh, I'm drowning too! Ask me when we're closer, then we can drown together."

mio.yes: Mio teaches history as a list of ghosts: who died where, who's still there. Your history is suddenly very good. You may never sleep again.
mio.no: "Hmm. You're not interesting enough yet. Come back with a ghost story."

hayate.ask: "Want me to drill you for the exams?"
hayate.yes: You drill Hayate on the steps outside the gym. He gets everything wrong, then everything right, then punches the air so hard he falls down two steps. "If I pass, I'm buying you ramen."

tutor.jealous: From the doorway, a hood. Amane watches you study with someone else and doesn't come in. The rain gets heavier.
tutor.done: "We already studied today. Go home and sleep, or it won't stick."

copy.post: Someone got caught copying in 2-B today. Zero on the paper. Guess who.

ranking.title: The {kind} results go up on the board outside the staff room.
ranking.top: Your name is in the top thirty. People who have never said your name before say it. You don't like it as much as you expected. You like it a bit.
ranking.mid: Somewhere in the middle. Invisible, exactly as planned. Somehow it doesn't feel like a plan.
ranking.low: Near the bottom. Hayate finds his name below yours and is delighted for both of you.
ranking.caught: Under your name, in Makabe-sensei's handwriting: (one paper void).
ranking.amane_good: Amane, behind you, very quietly: "I knew. I knew Senpai was clever." He takes a photo of the board.
ranking.amane_bad: Amane, behind you: "I'd still like Senpai if Senpai came 160th. I'd like Senpai more, actually. Fewer rivals."
ranking.hayate_taught: Hayate jumps on your back. "I PASSED. Everything! Ramen, Asagiri! I owe you ramen for LIFE!"
